newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA ROUT INDIA AGAIN TO CLINCH SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA ROUT INDIA AGAIN TO CLINCH SERIES.

text.p: South Africa moved closer to a series clean sweep against India after handing out a second humbling test defeat to Sachin Tendulkar's side in Cape Town on Monday.

India were bowled out for less than 150 for the third time in four innings to give South Africa a 282 run victory to complete a 2-0 series win with the third test to come in Johannesburg later this month.
With bowler Javagal Srinath absent with a cracked finger, South Africa wrapped up victory by hustling out India for 144 in just 66.2 overs with a combination of pace and spin.
Tendulkar admitted his side had problems to solve with this latest collapse following on innings of only 100 and 66 in losing the Christmas test in Durban by 328 runs.
"We just have to practise more on these bouncy tracks," he told reporters.
"We do get demoralised at times but these guys are young and they are all wanting to do well for the country.
"We are a young side with an average age of 24 or 25 and most of the guys have played only three or four tests and as far as I am concerned we just have to give them time.
"South Africa are one of the top sides in the world, very competitive, very professional and it's good that our young players have seen the tougher side of cricket at a young age."
India resumed on 52 for three with much depending on Tendulkar who had scored 169 in the first innings and was six not out overnight.
But in the fourth over of the morning he aimed a hook at a delivery wide of the off-stump from man of the match Brian McMillan to give a catch to mid on.

Four balls later Mohammad Azharuddin -- who made 115 in the first innings in a 222 partnership with his skipper to help avoid the follow-on -- drove airily at Allan Donald and was snapped up by third slip.
That left the Indian innings in tatters at 61 for five and although V.V.S Laxman hung around for two and a quarter hours for an undefeated 35, wickets fell regularly at the other end.

Doda Ganesh was bowled off a bottom edge by Donald with Paul Adams combining twice with keeper Dave Richardson to dismiss Anil Kumble and Venkatesh Prasad. The latter became Richardson's first stumping in his 33rd test to add to his 119 catches.
"It's a big help for me to have five bowlers as there is always one fresh who can keep the pressure on," South African skipper Hansie Cronje told reporters.
"I'm very happy with the team we have got -- it certainly feels like a world class unit.

"The difference between the sides is that we have four fast bowlers and while India have Srinath and Prasad -- certainly two of the top 10 in the world -- they have no-one to back them up and keep the pressure on."
South Africa's series win made up for their 2-1 series defeat in India last year, added Cronje.
"They gave us a bit of a hiding when they beat us 2-1 in India and I wouldn't mind doing it to them again in Johannesburg for the last test."
Srinath, who has a hairline fracture on the ring finger of his left hand, is expected to be fit for the third test in Johannesburg from January 16-20.
